findings.title: Edited attachment provenance can exclude imported product work from review
findings.reason: The new validator accepts SHA-shaped strings and any matching diff-base decision, not verified attachment provenance or the effective last diff-base. In a valid approved attachment, setting both x-delivery-base and x-base-commit to the imported HEAD passes validate and bundled implement receive (exit 0); scope then returns that HEAD and an empty product file set, dropping product/imported.mjs. Alternatively append a later diff-base at imported HEAD while retaining the original matching decision: validate/receive still pass and scope again loses imported work. An unrelated/nonexistent full x-imported-head also passes. Validate commit existence/ancestry and attachment delivery provenance, enforce that the effective review base remains the pinned delivery base across transitions, and add coordinated valid-SHA tampering and later-shadowing CLI regressions. Preserve the historical pinned base when remote refs advance rather than blindly recomputing it. Do not treat matching attacker-edited fields as proof.
x-evidence: node .context\compound-engineering\ce-review\attach-013\probe.mjs: paired-base mutation -> validation [], bundled receive code 0, scope files [].
Same probe: later-shadowing diff-base -> validation [], bundled receive code 0, scope files [].
Same probe: x-imported-head = 40 hexadecimal a characters -> validation [], bundled receive code 0.
The added tamper test only uses malformed SHA strings or a mismatched single decision; it does not cover coordinated valid-SHA mutations.
The claimed permanent provenance can also be removed after phase_completed becomes implement: the attachment validation branch no longer runs and validation succeeds.

findings.title: Initial attachment accepts a hand-forged approval without a fresh human action
findings.reason: The new initial-attachment invariant only requires gate.required=true and empty history. Starting from the never-approved init output, set gate.approved_by='repository owner' and gate.approved_at='2000-01-01'; leave updated_by='baton' and every other field unchanged. validate returns [] and bundled implement receive exits 0. The existing declarative role/date gate is newly used by this path without any attachment-specific fresh-approval evidence; record() deliberately omits all receipts for phase none, so even supported approval produces no independent receipt. This fails the requested forged-state rejection and fresh-approval requirement, rather than representing a cryptographic vulnerability claim. Add attachment-specific approval evidence bound to the attachment/source snapshot (without inventing completed phase history), validate it on receive, and test forged/stale approval as well as the supported approve path. If declarative role/date approval is intentionally the whole trust model, obtain an explicit scope decision narrowing the promised fail-closed contract instead of claiming forged approval is rejected.
x-evidence: Probe first verifies never-approved receive exits 3 with E_GATE_PENDING.
Probe restores the never-approved snapshot and writes only the configured role and old date; validation [], bundled receive code 0.
No prior human approval, approve CLI call for that snapshot, imported receipt, or human updated_by was present.
Existing role vocabulary validation is correct syntactically, but cannot establish the fresh action required by this newly introduced attachment path.
